sources.citation: Database and archive probes: Wikipedia 'Dumun language', Wikidata Q5314004, ANU Open Research search 'Dumun' (15 hits), archive.org advancedsearch 'Dumun Madang' (0 hits), transnewguinea.org/language/dumun (404), OLAC dui (empty), ELP lang/2157 (404), sil.org dui (an automated-access block), PARADISEC (error page), Usher newguineaworld Yaganon page (Google sign-in wall).
sources.note: No descriptive source for Dumun surfaced in any of them; the only works naming Dumun are the Z'graggen surveys, Claassen & McElhanon 1970, Ross 2019 and Wurm 2001.

sources.citation: Miklouho-Maclay, N. N. 2020 [1951]. Sobranie sochinenij, 2nd ed., vol. 3 (Bai wordlist pp. 158-163; commentary p. 402 equating Bai with Dumun).
sources.note: Bai column (c. 60 items, 1876-77) in Latin script with no stress marks and no prose on pronunciation; editors' table p. 402 maps 'Бай' to 'Думун' and 'Биби, Рай' to 'Думун (?)'. Glottolog and Ross 2019 treat Bai-Maclay as a distinct extinct language [baim1246].

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2019. A fragment of Papua New Guinea philology. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 37: 42-49 + appendix.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. fn. 2: 'Pawley & Hammarström use the label "Bai-Maclay" to distinguish it from Dumun, also referred to as "Bai" on the language map Z'graggen uses in all his Madang publications.' Analyses Maclay's 64-item Bai list as an extinct Yaganon outlier; contains no Dumun data.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2014. Ethnologue 17th ed., entry Dumun [dui] (the Internet Archive 2014 capture).
sources.note: Nothing. 'Alternate Names Bai. Population 35 (Wurm 2000). Location Madang Province, Astrolabe bay south coast, Gowar river mouth, west of Dein. Status 8b (Nearly extinct). Dialects None known. Related to Yabong, Ganglau, and Saep.' No resources beyond OLAC.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record Dumun [dumu1246] with its 5 references (Z'graggen 1975b; Wang 2005 [misattached: Bai of Yunnan]; Ethnologue 17; Moseley 2010; World Oral Literature Project).
sources.note: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; no descriptive reference of any kind.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A. 2001. Language endangerment in the insular Greater Pacific area, and the New Guinea area in particular. ANU handle 1885/254068.
sources.note: Endangerment survey listing Dumun; not a description (record seen in ANU search hits only).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress anywhere in the volume (a full-text search for stress/accent incl. scanned-spaced forms). pp. v-vi: 'Of Bx Dumun only a short word list was available to the present writer, but this list was sufficient to list Dumun as a member of the Yaganon family. Because of lack of data, Bx Dumun will be discarded in the remainder of this volume.' Note 5 (p. 173): 'Dumun is excluded from the remainder of this study.' No Dumun forms printed.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study Vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.3 Yaganon Family: Bai village lies 'in the Kulilau and Dumun area, which constituted a gap in the author's linguistic survey'; table entry 'Bx Dumun (Bai) 42'. Classification only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. p. 4: 'Short wordlists only were collected in Bx Dumun.. enough for a linguistic classification.' p. 14: 60-item Dumun-Kulilau list obtained April 1974 from a government official; Dumun differs from Ganglau in 40/60 words and is a separate language; only 10/28 of Maclay's Bai words cognate, so Bai is an extinct Yaganon language; 'Dumun is now marked as Bx instead of Bai.' Gazetteer: 42 speakers (Dumun 33, Kulilau 9). Classification and census only.

sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23.
sources.note: Sec. 3.4.2 (p. 61): Ganglau: 'A widely divergent dialect is reported to be spoken in the villages of Kulilau and Dumun to the west.' Sec. 6.1.1 (p. 63) Yaganon phonology: consonant remarks only. p. 66: stress sentences concern Rawa (phonemic), Yupna and Wantoat (probably sub-phonemic) and Suroi ('stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words'); nothing for Yaganon/Ganglau/Dumun.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. (unpublished). 60-item Dumun-Kulilau wordlist collected by a government official, April 1974 (the sole primary data on Dumun; cited PL B-41 p. 14 and PL D-30 note 5, never printed).
